curriculum.lesson_evidence: Australia is a multicultural society: First Nations Peoples and people with family links to many countries live here. Diversity includes languages, foods, arts and beliefs practised with respect.
curriculum.scope_limit: Proposed Stage 2 NESA HSIE alignment using catalogue outcome codes (HS2-*); content-point mapping and local First Nations protocols remain pending human review.

lesson.child_mission: Australia is a multicultural society: First Nations Peoples and people with family links to many countries live here. Diversity includes languages, foods, arts and beliefs practised with respect.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same HSIE idea to a new place or source, then compare two pieces of evidence for strength.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Why start with First Nations Peoples when describing Australia’s people?

FEEDBACK
They are the original peoples of this continent; multicultural stories sit alongside that truth.

WATCH FOR
Treating multiculturalism as only food festivals ignores rights, languages and First Nations status.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Make a respectful diversity web: First Nations + migrant contributions from published sources. No forced family sharing. List sources.

Write a short reflection naming one source or idea you corrected and why.
lesson.learning_intention: Australia is a multicultural society: First Nations Peoples and people with family links to many countries live here. Diversity includes languages, foods, arts and beliefs practised with respect.
materials: Optional: local map, photo or interview notes
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.
lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Make a respectful diversity web: First Nations + migrant contributions from published sources. No forced family sharing. List sources. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original response on new material: They are the original peoples of this continent; multicultural stories sit alongside that truth. Reasoning: I used multicultural by attending to diversity rather than copying the worked model.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Treating multiculturalism as only food festivals ignores rights, languages and First Nations status. Correction: They are the original peoples of this continent; multicultural stories sit alongside that truth. Why: the correction restores accurate use of multicultural.

Parent: Likely misconception: Treating multiculturalism as only food festivals ignores rights, languages and First Nations status. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating multicultural on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with multicultural, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

This helps the learner base claims on sources, places and respectful community knowledge, rather than guessing from a single picture. Keep every claim linked to evidence.
